CREATE TABLE products (
    sku_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    category VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    expected_shelf_zone VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    unit_price DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    priority VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE inventory (
    sku_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY,
    on_shelf_qty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (on_shelf_qty >= 0),
    backroom_qty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (backroom_qty >= 0),
    pos_last_hour_sales INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (pos_last_hour_sales >= 0),
    reorder_threshold INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (reorder_threshold >= 0),
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (sku_id) REFERENCES products(sku_id)
);

CREATE TABLE planogram (
    zone_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    expected_sku VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    expected_facings INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (expected_facings > 0),
    min_facings INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (min_facings > 0),
    promo_flag BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    PRIMARY KEY (zone_id, expected_sku),
    FOREIGN KEY (expected_sku) REFERENCES products(sku_id)
);

CREATE TABLE shelf_events (
    event_id VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    image_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    detected_issue VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    sku_id VARCHAR(32),
    confidence DECIMAL(4, 3) CHECK (confidence BETWEEN 0.0 AND 1.0),
    recommended_action TEXT NOT NULL,
    human_status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',
    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    captured_unit_price DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    captured_product_name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    approved_by VARCHAR(64),
    approved_at TIMESTAMP,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (sku_id) REFERENCES products(sku_id)
);

CREATE TABLE audit_logs (
    audit_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    actor_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    actor_role VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    action_category VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    target_resource VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    prior_state_hash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    new_state_hash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    payload_snapshot TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE traceability_matrix (
    requirement_id VARCHAR(16) PRIMARY KEY,
    requirement_text TEXT NOT NULL,
    story_reference VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    adr_reference VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    code_path VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    test_path VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    evidence_path VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
);

CREATE INDEX idx_shelf_events_status_created ON shelf_events(human_status, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_shelf_events_sku ON shelf_events(sku_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_planogram_zone ON planogram(zone_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_inventory_reorder ON inventory(sku_id, on_shelf_qty, reorder_threshold);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_timestamp ON audit_logs(timestamp DESC);

Database Architecture

ShelfGuard AI Database Design Specification

Version 2.0 | PostgreSQL 15+ Enterprise Schema Specification & Governance Design

Table of Contents

  1. Document Information
  2. Database Overview
  3. Entity Definitions
  4. Table Specifications
  5. Relationships & ERD
  6. Constraints & Validation
  7. Index Strategy
  8. Security & Auditing
  9. Data Retention & Archival

1. Document Information

Project NameShelfGuard AI
Target DBMSPostgreSQL 15+ / SQLite Compatible
AuthorPrincipal Database & AI Systems Architect
Security ClassificationEnterprise Confidential / Retail Operations

2. Database Overview

The ShelfGuard AI database schema is architected to support high-frequency asynchronous computer vision processing pipelines, real-time inventory synchronization, optimistic-locked human-in-the-loop task approvals, and immutable audit logging. Point-in-time financial snapshots are embedded directly within event records to prevent historical pricing drift during stockout revenue recovery calculations.

3. Entity Definitions

  • products: Master catalog of retail SKUs, categories, pricing, and assigned shelf zones.
  • inventory: Real-time tracking of on-shelf quantities, backroom stock, POS velocity, and reorder thresholds.
  • planogram: Expected facings, minimum facing bounds, and promotional flags per zone and SKU.
  • shelf_events: Log of computer vision anomaly detections with optimistic locking versioning and immutable point-in-time pricing snapshots.
  • audit_logs: Append-only security and operational trail tracking all administrative and human approval actions.
  • traceability_matrix: Links functional requirements (REQ-001 through REQ-008) to user stories, ADRs, source code paths, and test artifacts.

4. Table Specifications

products

Stores primary item master metadata.

ColumnTypeConstraintsDescription
sku_idVARCHAR(32)PRIMARY KEYUnique Stock Keeping Unit identifier
product_nameVARCHAR(128)NOT NULLDisplay name of the product
categoryVARCHAR(64)NOT NULLMerchandising category
expected_shelf_zoneVARCHAR(64)NOT NULLAssigned retail aisle and bay
unit_priceDECIMAL(10,2)NOT NULLMaster retail unit price
priorityVARCHAR(16)NOT NULLRestocking priority level

shelf_events

Captures CV anomalies, recommendations, and human approval states.

ColumnTypeConstraintsDescription
event_idVARCHAR(64)PRIMARY KEYUnique event identifier
human_statusVARCHAR(16)DEFAULT 'PENDING'Workflow state (PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED)
versionINTEGERNOT NULL DEFAULT 1Optimistic locking version counter
captured_unit_priceDECIMAL(10,2)NOT NULLPoint-in-time price snapshot for financial valuation

6. Constraints & Validation

  • Non-Negative Quantities: Inventory quantities (`on_shelf_qty`, `backroom_qty`, `pos_last_hour_sales`, `reorder_threshold`) must be $\ge 0$.
  • Confidence Bounds: CV confidence scores must fall between `0.0` and `1.0`.
  • Optimistic Locking: Approvals require strict version matching (`WHERE event_id = :id AND version = :v`) to prevent race conditions.

7. Index Strategy

Optimized B-tree path indexes are established for high-frequency queries:

  • idx_shelf_events_status_created: Accelerates pending task queue retrieval for store managers.
  • idx_inventory_reorder: Optimizes stock differential and reorder evaluation loops.
  • idx_audit_logs_timestamp: Ensures rapid append-only forensic log searches.

14. Security & Auditing

Database security enforces AES-256 storage encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit. All state-mutating actions (approvals, rejections, overrides) require explicit actor identification and write immutable delta snapshots to the audit_logs table.
